Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:10:1.english: By inference, that the first tanna, etc. - [This is asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:10:2.hebrew: אלומי אלמוה למילתא - דעדות, כשעשה הדבר ע"י השליח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:10:2.english: They strengthened the matter - [The matter] of testimony, when he performed the action through the agent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:10:3.hebrew: דינא רבה ודינא זוטא איכא בינייהו - לשמאי מיחייב בדינא רבה — בעונש גדול; ולת"ק לא מיענש כולי האי כהורג עצמו, אלא כגורם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:10:3.english: There is a great judgment and a small judgment between them - According to Shammai, [the sender] is liable to a great judgment — with a severe punishment; and according to the first tanna, he is not punished that much, like one who kills [the victim] himself, but rather as one who causes [it].

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:12:1.english: And my lord Joab - This is the rebellion, that he called him “lord” in the presence of the king.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:13:1.hebrew: אם ת"ל - דהאי חייב דקאמר שמאי, בדיני אדם קאמר, ויליף ממעילה וטביחה, וקסבר שני כתובים הבאים כאחד כו' — אפ"ה מודה הוא באומר כו', הואיל ונהנה שליח זה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:13:1.english: If you say - That this [ruling of] "liable" that Shammai stated, he stated [it with regard to liability] by the laws of man, and he derives [it] from [the cases of] *me'ilah* and *teviḥah*, and he maintains that two verses that come as one [teach a precedent], etc. — even so, he concedes in [the case of one who] says [to his agent: "Go and engage in sexual intercourse...", etc.], since this agent benefited.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:14:1.hebrew: שליח נעשה עד - בין לקידושין, בין ששלח ממון לבעל חובו — מצטרף שליח עם עד להיות שנים, או אם שניהם שלוחים היו ביחד, שניהם מעידים בדבר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:14:1.english: An agent can become a witness - Whether for betrothal or whether one sent money to his creditor — an agent combines with [another] witness to be two [witnesses], or if both of them were agents together, both of them testify about the matter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:14:2.hebrew: ה"נ דלא הוו קידושי - הרי ראו! וכי אמרינן בסנהדרין (דף כט.) צריך שיאמר "אתם עדיי" — ה"מ בעדי הודאה, שפעמים שאדם מודה לתובעו מנה, ואומר: "הדין עמך", מפני שרוצה להשתיקו מעליו עד לאחר זמן, ואע"פ שאינו חייב לו כלום. לפיכך, אין השומע יכול להעיד "בפני הודה", עד שיאמר "אתם עדי". אבל בעלמא — לא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:14:2.english: So too [would they hold] that it is not a betrothal - Behold, they saw [the act]! And when we say in Sanhedrin (29a) [that] he must say, "You are my witnesses," this applies [only] to witnesses of an admission, for sometimes a person admits [owing] a maneh to his claimant and says, "You are in the right," because he wants to silence him from [pressing] him until a later time, even though he owes him nothing. Therefore, the listener cannot testify, "He admitted before me," unless [the debtor] says, "You are my witnesses." But in general, [this is] not [required].

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:15:1.hebrew: אלומי אלמוה למילתא - דעדות, כשעשה הדבר ע"י השליח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:15:1.english: They strengthened the matter - [The matter] of testimony, when he performed the action through the agent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:17:1.english: He who said - [This refers to] Rav.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:17:2.english: An agent and one witness - Can testify about the matter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:17:3.english: Reverse - [Switch the opinion] of Beit Hillel to Beit Shammai [and that of Beit Shammai to Beit Hillel].

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:17:4.english: Taught the opposite - With regard to the dispute of the Amoraim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:17:5.english: And the halakha is that an agent can become a witness - [This] is our reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:18:1.english: They themselves are his witnesses - For an agent can become a witness.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:18:2.hebrew: וכן בגרושין - אם שלח גט לאשתו ע"י שנים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:18:2.english: And so too regarding divorce - If he sent a bill of divorce to his wife via two [people].

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:1:1.english: Let us derive from it - From [the case of] misuse of consecrated property.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:1:2.hebrew: מה מכירה - אינה מתקיימת אלא ע"י אחר — הגנב מוכר, והלוקח לוקח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:1:2.english: Just as a sale - It cannot take place except by means of another [person] — the thief sells and the buyer purchases.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:1:3.hebrew: אף טביחה - אפילו טבחה שליח, נתחייב הגנב בתשלומי ד' וה':
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:1:3.english: So too slaughter - Even if an agent slaughtered it, the thief is liable for the fourfold and fivefold payment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:2:1.english: Or sells it - To include even an agent.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:2:2.hebrew: תחת השור תחת השה - דחד מינייהו יתירה הוא, ודרוש לרבות: שאם מינה שליח תחתיו לטבוח, חייב הגנב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:2:2.english: For the ox, for the sheep - For one of them is superfluous, and it is expounded to include that if [the thief] appointed an agent in his stead to slaughter, the thief is liable.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:3:1.english: What can be said - Let us derive from it that there is an agent for a matter of transgression.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:3:2.english: He and not his agent - This is our reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:6:1.hebrew: ולמ"ד אין מלמדין - ולית לן למילף ממעילה וטביחה דיש שליח לדבר עבירה, ומסברא אין שליח, דאית לן למימר דיש לו לשמוע דברי הרב — והני ההוא ההוא, מאי דריש בהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:6:1.english: And according to the one who says [that two verses that come as one] do not teach - And [so] we do not derive from *me'ilah* [misuse of consecrated property] and *tevichah* [slaughter of a stolen animal] that there is agency for a transgression, and based on logical reasoning there is no agency, for we have to say that he [the agent] must listen to the words of the Master [rather than those of the student, the sender] — then [as for] these [terms], “that [man]” [and] “that [man],” what does he derive from them?

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:6:2.english: To exclude two who hold, etc. - That they are exempt from a sin-offering for slaughtering outside [the Temple courtyard].

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:6:3.english: “That [man]” — but not one who is compelled - For “that [man]” implies that he must be in his [normal] state and in a settled frame of mind.

Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:9:1.hebrew: קסבר שני כתובים הבאים כאחד מלמדים - ויליף ממעילה וטביחה דיש שליח לדבר עבירה. והני ״ההוא״ דריש להו: חד למעוטי שנים אוחזים, וחד למעוטי אנוס; ולית ליה דרשה ד״הוא״ ״ההוא״:
Rashi on Kiddushin 43a:9:1.english: He holds that two verses that come as one teach [a precedent] - And he derives from [the cases of] misuse [of consecrated property] and slaughter [of a stolen animal] that there is agency for transgression. And these [instances of the word] “that [man]” [hahu], he expounds them: one to exclude two who hold [a knife and slaughter], and one to exclude [one who was] compelled; and he does not accept the exposition of “hu” [versus] “hahu”.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:10:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא פליגי אלא כו' - תימה: אמאי קאמר "עד כאן לא פליגי"? כי נמי פליגי, מי לא פריך שפיר ממילתיה דב"ה?! וי"ל: היינו טעמא דלא רצה למיפרך מב"ה — דהוה מצי לשנויי "איפוך", כדמשני בסמוך:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:10:1.english: “They disagree only...” - [It is] surprising: Why does [the Gemara] say, “They disagree only...”? Even if they [also] disagree [with regard to two], does it not refute [Rav] well from the statement of Beit Hillel?! And one can say: That is the reason [the Gemara] did not want to refute [Rav] from [the statement of] Beit Hillel — for it would have been able to answer: “Reverse [the opinions],” as it answers nearby.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:12:1.hebrew: מורד במלכות הוה דקאמר ליה ואדוני יואב כו' - פי' בקונטרס: דמורד היה מהא דקאמר "אדוני יואב" בפני המלך דוד. ולא נהירא, שהרי יואב לא היה מורד במלכות. ואומר רבינו מאיר, אביו של ר"ת: מה שאמר לו דוד שילך לביתו לאכול ולשתות, והוא מיאן בדבר — כדכתיב: "כל עבדי אדוני על פני השדה חונים, ואני אבא אל ביתי לאכול וגו'", בתמיה — ולא היה לו לסרב. וי"מ: דהמרד היה שהקדים לומר "אדוני יואב" קודם המלך דוד:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:12:1.english: "He was a rebel against the monarchy, as he said to him: 'And my lord Joab, etc.'" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres that he was a rebel because he said "my lord Joab" in the presence of King David. But this is not tenable, as Joab was not a rebel against the monarchy. And Rabbeinu Meir, the father of Rabbeinu Tam, says: [The rebellion was regarding] that which David told him to go to his house to eat and drink, and he refused the matter — as it is written: "All the servants of my lord are encamped in the open field, and shall I enter my house to eat, etc.?!", as a rhetorical question — and he should not have refused [the king's command]. And some explain that the rebellion was that he mentioned "my lord Joab" before King David.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:13:1.hebrew: שלא מצינו בכל התורה כולה זה נהנה וזה מתחייב - וא"ת: והא איכא מעילה, שאם אמר הגזבר לשליח: "אכול ככר זה של הקדש", והשליח לא ידע שהוא של הקדש — דחייב המשלח; ואמאי? "זה נהנה וזה מתחייב" הוא! וי"ל: דמעילה, לא מתחייב המשלח ע"י הנאת השליח, אלא ע"י הגבהה דשליח — דמיד דאגבהיה שליח קנייה, וההיא שעתא חייב משלח. אמנם מסופק היה ר"י באומר לשליח: "הושט ידך לכד של שמן ותהנה מן הסיכה", או "שב על עורות של הקדש", או "התחמם בגיזי עולה", והשליח לא ידע דהם של הקדש — דהשתא לא עשאו שליח אלא מן ההנאה — אם יתחייב המשלח כדאמרינן גבי מעילה, או דילמא "זה נהנה וזה מתחייב" לא אמרינן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:13:1.english: "For we have not found in the entire Torah [that] this one benefits and that one is liable" - And if you say: But isn't there [the case of] me'ilah [misappropriation of consecrated property]? For if the treasurer said to an agent, "Eat this loaf of consecrated property," and the agent did not know that it was of consecrated property, the sender is liable! And why? It is [a case where] this one benefits and that one is liable! And one can say: That [in the case of] me'ilah, the sender does not become liable through the agent's benefit, but rather through the agent's lifting [of the loaf]; for as soon as the agent lifted it, he acquired it, and at that moment the sender became liable. However, the Ri was in doubt in [a case where] one says to an agent: "Reach your hand into a jug of oil and benefit from anointing," or: "Sit on hides of consecrated property," or: "Warm yourself with the shearings of a burnt-offering," and the agent did not know that they were of consecrated property — where now he only appointed him an agent for the benefit — whether the sender is liable, as we say regarding me'ilah, or perhaps we do not say [that] "this one benefits and that one is liable" [and therefore the sender is exempt].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:14:1.hebrew: ולא אמר להם אתם עדי ה"נ דלא הוו קידושי - ופשיטא דהוו קידושין; משמע דלא מצרכי לומר "אתם עדיי" כי אם בהודאה, כדאמר בסנהדרין (דף כט.), שאם אמר לחבירו: "אתה חייב לי מנה", והודה בפני שנים — אם לא אמר אחד מהם "אתם עדיי", יכול לומר לו היום או למחר: "משטה אני בך". מיהו, אי לא טעין — לא טענינן ליה; אבל עשוי אדם שלא להשביע עצמו — כגון אם הודה הלוה בפני שנים: "חייב אני לך", בלא תביעת המלוה — טענינן ליה, אפי' כי לא טען:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:14:1.english: "And [did] not say to them: 'You are my witnesses,' so too is it not a betrothal?" - And it is obvious that it is [a valid] betrothal; [this] implies that they do not require [one] to say "You are my witnesses" except in [the case of an] admission [of debt], as [the Gemara] says in Sanhedrin (29a): that if one said to his fellow, "You owe me a maneh," and he admitted [it] in the presence of two [witnesses] — if neither of them [the claimant or the debtor] said, "You are my witnesses," he can say to him today or tomorrow, "I was jesting with you." However, if [the debtor] does not plead [this], we [the court] do not plead [it] on his behalf; but [regarding the rationale that] a person is prone not to appear sated [with wealth] — such as if the debtor admitted in the presence of two [witnesses], "I owe you," without a claim [having been made by] the creditor — we [the court] plead [it] on his behalf, even when he did not plead [it himself].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:16:1.hebrew: עד כאן לא פליגי אלא כו' - תימה: אמאי קאמר "עד כאן לא פליגי"? כי נמי פליגי — מי לא פריך שפיר ממילתיה דב"ה? וי"ל: היינו טעמא דלא רצה למיפרך מב"ה — דהוה מצי לשנויי "איפוך", כדמשני בסמוך:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 43a:16:1.english: "They disagree only with regard to, etc." - [It is] puzzling: Why did [the Gemara] say, "They disagree only [with regard to three]"? Even if they [also] disagree, does it not raise a valid objection from the statement of Beit Hillel? And one can say: This is the reason that [the Gemara] did not want to object from Beit Hillel — because it could have answered: "Reverse [the opinions]," as [the Gemara] answers nearby.
